diagram.manim_description: Canvas 16 by 9 units (16:9), origin at the centre, x to the right, y up, plain BG white, no frame, no title. Each band has a rounded rectangle label box at the left (x from -7.6 to -5.4, height 0.95, corner radius 0.15, INK outline 2 px, BG fill) holding two centred text lines 0.30 units high. Band 1: label box centre y = 2.93 with the lines 'Regular' and 'Polygons'. Draw 8 regular polygons, each of circumradius 0.32, fill CELL_FILL, INK outline, with n vertices at angles t0 + k x (360 / n) degrees (k = 0 to n - 1) around its centre, where t0 = 90 for n = 3, 5, 7 and 9, t0 = 45 for n = 4, t0 = 0 for n = 6 and 10, t0 = 22.5 for n = 8. Sub-row 1 has centre y = 3.70 and centres x = -4.2, -1.45, 1.3, 4.05: triangle (n = 3), quadrilateral (n = 4, a square), pentagon (n = 5), hexagon (n = 6). Sub-row 2 has centre y = 2.55 and the same four x values: heptagon (n = 7), octagon (n = 8), nonagon (n = 9), decagon (n = 10). Write each polygon's name under it, centred on its x, 0.30 units high: at y = 3.15 for sub-row 1 (Triangle, Quadrilateral, Pentagon, Hexagon) and at y = 2.00 for sub-row 2 (Heptagon, Octagon, Nonagon, Decagon). Band 2: label box centre y = 0.75 with the lines 'Complete' and 'Graphs'. Draw the complete graphs K2, K3, K4, K5, K6 at centres x = -4.2, -2.0, 0.2, 2.4, 4.6 and centre y = 0.95. Each has its n vertices on a circle of radius 0.45 at angles t0 + k x (360 / n) degrees (K2: t0 = 0, so the vertices are at the left and right ends of a horizontal segment; K3: t0 = 90; K4: t0 = 45; K5: t0 = 90; K6: t0 = 0), a filled INK dot of radius 0.05 at every vertex, and an INK straight segment joining every pair of its vertices. Write the italic labels K2, K3, K4, K5, K6 under the graphs, centred on each graph's x, at y = 0.25, 0.30 units high. Band 3: label box centre y = -0.71 with the lines 'Stacked' and 'Squares'. Draw five square grids with no fill and INK lines: the n-th grid (n = 1 to 5) is n by n little squares of side 0.17 (so n x 0.17 wide and tall), its bottom edge on y = -1.22, centred on x = -4.2, -2.0, 0.2, 2.4, 4.6. Band 4: label box centre y = -2.03 with the lines 'Stacked' and 'Triangles'. Draw five equilateral triangles with the apex up, INK lines, no fill, centred on the same five x values with the base on y = -2.54: the n-th triangle (n = 1 to 5) has base 0.1963 x n and height 0.17 x n and is divided into n rows of little equilateral triangles of side 0.1963 by n - 1 further lines parallel to each of its three sides, spaced one little-triangle height apart. Band 5: label box centre y = -3.35 with the lines 'Koch' and 'Snowflake'. Draw five Koch-snowflake stages with INK outline and no fill, centroid at y = -3.35 and x = -4.2, -2.0, 0.2, 2.4, 4.6. Stage 0 is an equilateral triangle whose vertices are at distance 0.55 from the centroid at angles 180, 300 and 60 degrees (one corner points left and one side is vertical on the right). Each next stage replaces every segment of the previous stage by four equal segments: the first third, the two sides of an equilateral triangle built outwards on the middle third, and the last third. The five stages have 3, 12, 48, 192 and 768 segments. Draw no numbers anywhere and keep the area with x greater than 5.3 empty.

items.question_text: To get from one shape to the next shape in the Koch Snowflake sequence, one replaces each line segment by a 'speed bump'. As one does this more and more times, the changes become tinier and tinier with very very small line segments. How many total line segments are there in each shape of the Koch Snowflake? What is the corresponding number sequence? (The answer is 3, 12, 48, ..., i.e., 3 times Powers of 4; this sequence is not shown in Table 1.)
items.reason: The rule 'replace each segment by a speed bump' is given only as a small drawing inside the book question, and the five Koch shapes exist only in the picture (Table 3, fifth row); both are needed to count the segments.
